Re-analysis of a marine plastic-substrate metaproteome

This is a second, independent test of the same comparison case_study.Rmd ran on the diet metaproteome: does a TM-Vec ground metric (weightedRep()) find sample-level structure that protein-identity distances (Bray-Curtis, Jaccard) miss or dilute, and does collapsing proteins into structural bins (rollupStructural()) surface a substrate-associated bin that a per-protein test would drown in multiple testing? The dataset here is a marine plastic-incubation metaproteome: 24 samples as collected, eight substrates, three replicate incubations each – four plastics (PHBV, PLA, HDPE, a PLA/PCL blend), two PHBH formulations (“PHBH” and “PHBH Green”), filter paper (a fast-degrading cellulose control), and sediment (the ambient community, no added substrate). One substrate, PLA, is dropped for depth reasons below, leaving seven.

It differs from the diet study in one way that matters throughout: replicates are independent incubations, not repeated samples of the same subject, so there is no blocking factor in the permutation tests below.

Sys.setenv(KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK = "TRUE")
reticulate::use_python(Sys.which("python3"), required = TRUE)

library(phyloseq)
library(vegan)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)
library(here)
library(MicrobiomeStat)
for (f in list.files("R", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)

path  <- here("data", "case_study2")
NPERM <- 9999

Data

ps <- readRDS(file.path(path, "ps.rds"))   # built and validated in data_curation_case_study2.Rmd
ps

Rarefaction

Depth here is nothing like the diet study’s: that report’s shallowest samples sat within a few percent of each other, so the rarefaction floor was just min(). Here total counts span roughly 90 to 25,700 across the 24 samples, close to 300-fold.

depth <- data.frame(sample = sample_names(ps), depth = sample_sums(ps),
                    substrate = data.frame(sample_data(ps))$substrate)
depth <- depth[order(depth$depth), ]
depth$sample <- factor(depth$sample, levels = depth$sample)

ggplot(depth, aes(sample, depth, fill = substrate)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "sample, sorted by depth", y = "total counts (rounded PUP)") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

PLA’s three replicates were each searched against a similarly large protein catalog (27641, 27737, 27919 proteins offered, B1/B2/B3) – so this is not a case of one replicate having less evidence available to it. What came back differs enormously within that shared search space: 46, 325, 829 proteins actually detected, an 18-fold range across three replicates of the same substrate. The low end of that range is a failed or badly degraded run, not ordinary replicate noise, and it is not obvious from depth alone which of the other two are trustworthy either. Rather than keep the substrate at reduced, uncertain replication, or let its worst replicate set the floor for all 21 other samples, the whole substrate is dropped.

ps <- prune_samples(data.frame(sample_data(ps))$substrate != "PLA", ps)
ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps) > 0, ps)
sample_data(ps)$substrate <- droplevels(sample_data(ps)$substrate)
floor_depth <- min(sample_sums(ps))    # rarefy to the shallowest remaining sample, dropping none of the rest
c(samples_remaining = nsamples(ps), floor_depth = floor_depth)
## samples_remaining       floor_depth 
##                21               655

The floor (655) now comes from S2, a sediment replicate – shallow, but not an isolated outlier the way PLA was: the next five samples after it sit within a similar few-thousand-count range, so there is no second cut to make.

psd <- rarefy_even_depth(ps, sample.size = floor_depth, rngseed = 1,
                         replace = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
psd <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(psd) > 0, psd)
md  <- data.frame(sample_data(psd))
psd
## phyloseq-class experiment-level object
## otu_table()   OTU Table:         [ 5262 taxa and 21 samples ]
## sample_data() Sample Data:       [ 21 samples by 3 sample variables ]
## tax_table()   Taxonomy Table:    [ 5262 taxa by 9 taxonomic ranks ]
## refseq()      AAStringSet:      [ 5262 reference sequences ]

Embedding

TM-Vec1, same model and reasoning as case_study.Rmd: its head regresses the TM-score of protein pairs, so cosine similarity between two vectors is a predicted TM-score. The cache is keyed by exact sequence and model, so a stale vector from a re-curated sequence or a different model can’t be silently reused.

model_tag <- eval(formals(embed_proteins)$model)
cache <- file.path(path, "embeddings_tmvec1_large.rds")
cached <- if (file.exists(cache)) readRDS(cache) else list(Z = NULL, seq = character(0), model = character(0))

# keyed off ps (unrarefied, PLA already dropped), not psd -- covers every protein
# either count matrix below could need, rarefied or not
full_seq <- stats::setNames(as.character(refseq(ps)[taxa_names(ps)]), taxa_names(ps))

reusable <- intersect(taxa_names(ps), rownames(cached$Z))
reusable <- reusable[cached$seq[reusable] == full_seq[reusable] &
                      cached$model[reusable] == model_tag]
need  <- setdiff(taxa_names(ps), reusable)
Zall  <- cached$Z

if (length(need)) {
  s <- substr(full_seq[need], 1, 1022)
  s <- s[order(nchar(s))]
  for (i in split(seq_along(s), ceiling(seq_along(s) / 2000))) {
    new_Z <- embed_proteins(s[i], batch_size = 16)
    Zall  <- rbind(Zall[setdiff(rownames(Zall), rownames(new_Z)), , drop = FALSE], new_Z)
    cached$Z <- Zall
    cached$seq[rownames(new_Z)]   <- full_seq[rownames(new_Z)]
    cached$model[rownames(new_Z)] <- model_tag
    saveRDS(cached, cache)
  }
}
Z      <- Zall[taxa_names(ps), ]
cnt    <- t(as(otu_table(psd), "matrix"))   # samples in rows, RAREFIED -- distances/PCoA only
cnt_da <- t(as(otu_table(ps), "matrix"))    # samples in rows, UNRAREFIED -- differential abundance only
length_abundance_profile(cnt, full_seq, max_length = 1022) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 1300, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey30")

At the 1022aa line (dashed), 4.4% of the catalog by count sits past it, and it carries 3.8% of total abundance – unlike the diet study, abundance here does not run ahead of protein count past the cutoff, so there is no specific large-protein-family enrichment to call out. The same argument from case_study.Rmd for trusting truncated embeddings (abundance-weighted aggregation over thousands of proteins) applies here too; 1300 is marked for reference but no bin-level analysis in this report depends on it.

Accession sharing

Bray-Curtis and Jaccard can only track substrate through accessions two samples literally share. Unlike the diet study – one mouse colony searched against one shared protein database, where accession sharing was close to universal – every sample here comes from its own per-sample metagenome assembly, so an accession is only ever shared when the same protein happened to assemble and get called independently in more than one sample.

pres <- cnt > 0
n_shared <- colSums(pres)
n_substrates <- vapply(seq_len(ncol(cnt)), function(j) length(unique(md$substrate[pres[, j]])), integer(1))

gt(data.frame(
  quantity = c("proteins detected in exactly 1 sample",
              "proteins detected in >1 sample",
              "proteins detected in >1 substrate"),
  n = c(sum(n_shared == 1), sum(n_shared > 1), sum(n_substrates > 1)),
  pct = round(100 * c(mean(n_shared == 1), mean(n_shared > 1), mean(n_substrates > 1)), 1)))
quantity n pct
proteins detected in exactly 1 sample 4090 77.7
proteins detected in >1 sample 1172 22.3
proteins detected in >1 substrate 860 16.3

So this dataset sits between the diet study’s two extremes: not the near-universal accession sharing that let Bray-Curtis and Jaccard match TM-Vec1’s PERMANOVA there, and not the fully private-accession regime the diet study’s shuffle test constructed artificially. A meaningful minority of the catalog is shared across substrates, so protein-identity distances have real signal available to them here, not none.

Results

# Weighted UniFrac on a structure tree fitted to the TM-Vec ground metric.
# UPGMA (fastcluster, O(n^2)); BIONJ fits a non-additive metric better but is
# O(n^3) and takes hours at this protein count.
G_tm <- tmDist(Z[colnames(cnt), , drop = FALSE])
tree_tm <- structureTree(G_tm, method = "upgma")
tree_fidelity <- cor(as.vector(G_tm),
                     as.vector(as.dist(ape::cophenetic.phylo(tree_tm)[labels(G_tm), labels(G_tm)])))

D <- list(`Bray-Curtis` = phyloseq::distance(psd, method = "bray"),
          `Jaccard`     = vegdist(cnt, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE),
          `weightedRep` = weightedRep(cnt, G_tm, method = "unifrac", tree = tree_tm))

No nuisance covariates and no permutation blocking: each sample is an independent incubation replicate, not a repeated measurement of the same unit.

substrate_test <- function(dl, nperm = NPERM) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(dl), function(n) {
  set.seed(1)
  a <- adonis2(dl[[n]] ~ substrate, data = md, by = "terms", permutations = nperm)
  data.frame(distance = n, R2 = round(a["substrate", "R2"], 3),
             F = round(a["substrate", "F"], 2), p = a["substrate", "Pr(>F)"])
}))
res <- substrate_test(D)
r2  <- setNames(res$R2, res$distance)
gt(res)
distance R2 F p
Bray-Curtis 0.437 1.81 1e-04
Jaccard 0.364 1.34 1e-04
weightedRep 0.541 2.75 1e-04
 
for (n in names(D)) {
  print(plot_ordination(psd, ordinate(psd, "PCoA", distance = D[[n]]), color = "substrate") +
          stat_ellipse(type = "t", geom = "polygon", alpha = 0) +
          ggtitle(n) + theme_bw())
}

Diagnostics

gt(data.frame(
  distance     = names(D),
  betadisper_p = sapply(D, function(d) {
    bd <- betadisper(d, md$substrate, bias.adjust = TRUE)
    round(permutest(bd, permutations = NPERM)$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1], 4)
  }),
  row.names = NULL))
distance betadisper_p
Bray-Curtis 0.1565
Jaccard 0.2470
weightedRep 0.7828

Differential abundance

Unrarefied counts (cnt_da, from ps), not the rarefied cnt the sections above use. Rarefaction earns its keep for a sample-level distance – Bray-Curtis and weightedRep need every sample on the same footing, and subsampling is the standard way to buy that. A per-bin model doesn’t have the same need: LinDA fits its own bias-corrected centered-log-ratio transform per sample, which already absorbs each sample’s own depth, so throwing away real counts on top of that would trade statistical power for nothing (McMurdie & Holmes, PLoS Comp Biol 2014, arguing rarefaction is broadly the wrong tool for differential-abundance testing specifically, as opposed to beta-diversity). At this dataset’s aggressive floor (655, from dropping PLA) that power is real: unrarefied keeps 30997 proteins against 5262 rarefied, and every member below still gets a fair shot at clearing LinDA’s own zero-handling rather than being subsampled to zero before the model ever sees it.

PERMANOVA says substrate structures the community overall; it says nothing about which proteins carry that signal. Testing all 30997 proteins directly would run that many near-independent tests on units that mostly are not independent – proteins with similar structure are frequently near-homologous, so a chunk of those “tests” repeat the same signal. rollupStructural() collapses proteins into bins where every member has predicted TM-score above a threshold to every other member; both the conventional TM-score same-fold boundary (0.5, Xu & Zhang 2010, used to pick the embedding model above) and a stricter cutoff (0.7, tighter and more homogeneous bins at the cost of more of them) are run below, as two independent passes over the same counts and embeddings – multiplicity is paid once per structural unit within each pass, not once per accession, but the two passes are not compared to each other statistically, only side by side.

roll_both <- rollupStructural_thresholds(cnt_da, Z, cluster_threshold = c(0.5, 0.7))

rollupStructural_thresholds() builds the pairwise TM-Vec distance matrix and its linkage tree once and cuts it at both heights, rather than paying that cost (the slow part; the cut itself is nearly free) twice over for two separate rollupStructural() calls.

is_annotated <- function(t) !is.na(t$MantisName) | !is.na(t$MicrobeName) |
  (!is.na(t$PlasticDB) & t$PlasticDB != "-") | !is.na(t$Depolymerase)
tax_all <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"))
flagged <- stats::setNames(
  !is.na(tax_all$PlasticDB) & tax_all$PlasticDB != "-" | !is.na(tax_all$Depolymerase),
  rownames(tax_all))

TM-score >= 0.5

roll_05 <- roll_both[["0.5"]]
c(proteins = ncol(cnt_da), bins = ncol(roll_05$counts))
## proteins     bins 
##    30997     1887

LinDA (Zhou et al., Genome Biology 2022) fits a linear model per bin on centered-log-ratio-transformed abundance and corrects the compositional bias a plain lm() on relative abundance would carry – the same reason weightedRep() works on abundance weights rather than raw proportions directly. feature.dat.type = "count" since roll_05$counts is still integer PUP counts, just not rarefied ones – the same choice case_study.Rmd makes on its own unrarefied PSM counts below. No random effect in the formula, unlike the diet study’s (1 | subject) – these are independent incubation replicates, not repeated samples of the same unit.

273 of 1887 bins here are nonzero in fewer than 3 of 21 samples, LinDA’s own stated bar for “virtually no statistical power” – prev.filter drops them before fitting rather than after, standard practice independent of anything specific to this bin count: at 1887 bins this fit is fast and small regardless of whether they are filtered (contrast the stricter threshold below, where the same filter is also what keeps the fit from running out of memory).

fit_05 <- linda(t(roll_05$counts), md, formula = "~ substrate",
               feature.dat.type = "count", prev.filter = 3 / nrow(roll_05$counts), verbose = FALSE)

substrate has 7 levels (sediment as the reference), so a single coefficient is not “the” substrate effect any more than it was for the diet study’s five-level diet term. The Wald test below is the same joint test on all 6 substrate coefficients per bin that adonis2’s by = "terms" gives at the sample level, now run per structural bin.

k <- nlevels(md$substrate) - 1
L <- matrix(0, nrow = k, ncol = length(fit_05$variables) + 1)
for (i in 1:k) L[i, i + 1] <- 1   # intercept + the k substrate dummy columns
wald_05 <- linda.wald.test(fit_05, L, model = "LM", alpha = 0.05)
rownames(wald_05) <- rownames(fit_05$output[[1]])   # linda.wald.test drops them; reused below

gt(data.frame(bins_tested = nrow(wald_05), bins_substrate_sig = sum(wald_05$reject),
              fraction_sig = round(mean(wald_05$reject), 3)))
bins_tested bins_substrate_sig fraction_sig
1614 517 0.32

32% of bins reject at padj <= 0.05. One log2 fold change per point needs one reference level; the 6 substrate-vs-Sediment contrasts already inside fit_05 are shown separately, one panel per non-reference substrate, red where that specific contrast rejects at padj <= 0.05.

substrate_vars_05 <- grep("^substrate", fit_05$variables, value = TRUE)
volc_05 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(substrate_vars_05, function(v) {
  o <- fit_05$output[[v]]
  data.frame(bin = rownames(o), substrate = sub("^substrate", "", v),
             log2FoldChange = o$log2FoldChange, pvalue = o$pvalue, reject = o$reject)
}))

ggplot(volc_05, aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(pvalue), color = reject)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ substrate, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey70", `TRUE` = "firebrick"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change vs Sediment", y = expression(-log[10](p))) + theme_bw()

top_05 <- volc_05[volc_05$reject, ]
top_05 <- top_05[which.max(abs(top_05$log2FoldChange)), ]

members_05 <- names(roll_05$bin)[roll_05$bin == top_05$bin]
tax_05 <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"))[members_05, ]
n_annotated_05    <- sum(is_annotated(tax_05))
n_multi_genome_05 <- sum(!is.na(tax_05$SharedGenomes))

The single largest shift, in either direction, is bin bin2 on PHBH Green vs. sediment: +9.5 log2 fold change at \(p =\) 9.9e-04. Its 83 members carry no shared lineage (this workbook has no GTDB call, data_curation_case_study2.Rmd), and 83 of 83 carries any curated call at all (MantisName, MicrobeName, a PlasticDB hit, or a depolymerase flag) – the table below has the specifics. rollupStructural_thresholds() grouped them by predicted fold alone, with no access to any of that either way, including which GenomeID (MAG) a member’s own sample assembly placed it in – not to be confused with this bin itself, a structural cluster; the two “bin” concepts are unrelated, see data_curation_case_study2.Rmd § One genome per protein. 41 of the 83 members were independently assembled and binned in more than one sample’s GenomeID (the SharedGenomes column below).

info_05 <- data.frame(
  Protein = members_05,
  `Genome ID` = tax_05$GenomeID,
  `Shared genomes` = tax_05$SharedGenomes,
  `Mantis annotation` = tax_05$MantisName,
  `Microbe annotation` = tax_05$MicrobeName,
  PlasticDB = tax_05$PlasticDB,
  `Possible depolymerase` = tax_05$Depolymerase,
  `Length (aa)` = nchar(full_seq[members_05]),
  `Mean count, Sediment` = round(colMeans(cnt_da[md$substrate == "Sediment", members_05, drop = FALSE]), 2),
  check.names = FALSE
)
info_05[[paste0("Mean count, ", top_05$substrate)]] <-
  round(colMeans(cnt_da[md$substrate == top_05$substrate, members_05, drop = FALSE]), 2)
peak_05 <- pmax(info_05[["Mean count, Sediment"]], info_05[[paste0("Mean count, ", top_05$substrate)]])
info_05 <- info_05[order(-peak_05), ]   # re-used below, so the sort has to stick
peak_05 <- sort(peak_05, decreasing = TRUE)
gt(info_05)

driver_05 <- info_05$Protein[1]
driver_annotated_05 <- is_annotated(tax_05[driver_05, ])
driver_desc_05 <- if (driver_annotated_05) {
  "does carry a curated call in this workbook -- see the table above for which one"
} else {
  "carries no `MantisName`, `MicrobeName`, `PlasticDB` or depolymerase call in this workbook"
}

top_share_05     <- peak_05[1] / sum(peak_05)
n_substantial_05 <- sum(peak_05 >= 0.1 * peak_05[1])
concentrated_05  <- top_share_05 >= 0.5

spread_desc_05 <- if (concentrated_05) {
  sprintf("It sits almost entirely in %s, detected in %d of 3 %s replicates and %d of 3 sediment replicates; the other %d members are near-zero traces in every sample, %s included, and contribute negligibly to the bin's summed abundance -- that protein %s%s.",
          driver_05,
          sum(cnt_da[md$substrate == top_05$substrate, driver_05] > 0), top_05$substrate,
          sum(cnt_da[md$substrate == "Sediment", driver_05] > 0),
          length(members_05) - 1, top_05$substrate, driver_desc_05,
          if (driver_annotated_05) "" else " -- the cleanest substrate-specific signal this differential-abundance pass found is also a member this workbook's own annotation pipeline said nothing about")
} else {
  sprintf("It is spread across the bin rather than concentrated in one protein: %s is the single largest contributor (%.0f%% of the bin's peak abundance) but %d of the %d members each reach at least a tenth of that -- a coherent multi-member signal, not a single-protein artifact. Its largest contributor %s%s.",
          driver_05, 100 * top_share_05, n_substantial_05, length(members_05), driver_desc_05,
          if (driver_annotated_05) "" else " -- unusual for a bin this well-supported; most of this workbook's dark proteins turn up alone, not as part of a mostly-annotated family")
}

Sorted by each member’s peak abundance, on whichever side of the contrast it is larger, the table shows the bin’s fold change: It is spread across the bin rather than concentrated in one protein: 15-2DG3_k141_360597_99 is the single largest contributor (13% of the bin’s peak abundance) but 21 of the 83 members each reach at least a tenth of that – a coherent multi-member signal, not a single-protein artifact. Its largest contributor does carry a curated call in this workbook – see the table above for which one.

rollupStructural_thresholds()’s complete-linkage guarantee is that every pair inside a bin has predicted TM-score >= 0.5 to every other member, not just a nearest neighbor – true here by construction, but a heatmap shows what it looks like: the full pairwise predicted TM-score matrix for bin bin2, same protein order as the table above.

Zb_05 <- Z[info_05$Protein, ]
S_05  <- 1 - as.matrix(proxy::dist(Zb_05, method = "cosine"))   # cosine == predicted TM-score
dimnames(S_05) <- list(info_05$Protein, info_05$Protein)

df_05 <- as.data.frame(as.table(S_05))
names(df_05) <- c("i", "j", "TM_hat")
df_05$i <- factor(df_05$i, levels = info_05$Protein, labels = seq_along(info_05$Protein))
df_05$j <- factor(df_05$j, levels = info_05$Protein, labels = seq_along(info_05$Protein))

ggplot(df_05, aes(i, j, fill = TM_hat)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0.5, 1), name = "predicted\nTM-score") +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(x = "protein, table row above", y = "protein, table row above") +
  theme_minimal()

The floor is 0.585, comfortably above the 0.5 cutoff, and the diagonal is exactly 1 by construction (cos(z, z) = 1).

sig_members_05 <- names(roll_05$bin)[roll_05$bin %in% rownames(wald_05)[wald_05$reject]]

gt(data.frame(
  scope = c("whole protein universe", "substrate-significant bins only"),
  proteins = c(ncol(cnt_da), length(sig_members_05)),
  plasticdb_or_depolymerase_flag = c(sum(flagged[colnames(cnt_da)]), sum(flagged[sig_members_05])),
  pct = round(100 * c(mean(flagged[colnames(cnt_da)]), mean(flagged[sig_members_05])), 2)))
scope proteins plasticdb_or_depolymerase_flag pct
whole protein universe 30997 270 0.87
substrate-significant bins only 18209 150 0.82

TM-score >= 0.7

roll_07 <- roll_both[["0.7"]]
c(proteins = ncol(cnt_da), bins = ncol(roll_07$counts))
## proteins     bins 
##    30997     7164

Same model as the 0.5 pass above, on a different (stricter, more numerous) set of bins.

3925 of 7164 bins here are nonzero in fewer than 3 of 21 samples, LinDA’s own stated bar for “virtually no statistical power.” Testing them anyway is not just wasted power: fitting every bin as one joint model (model = "LM", no random effect to loop over) makes its covariance matrix scale with bin count squared, and at the full 7164 – unlike the looser threshold above – it exceeds this machine’s memory outright. prev.filter drops them before fitting rather than after – the same features LinDA’s own warning already flags as underpowered, just excluded up front instead of tested and ignored.

fit_07 <- linda(t(roll_07$counts), md, formula = "~ substrate",
               feature.dat.type = "count", prev.filter = 3 / nrow(roll_07$counts), verbose = FALSE)
k <- nlevels(md$substrate) - 1
L <- matrix(0, nrow = k, ncol = length(fit_07$variables) + 1)
for (i in 1:k) L[i, i + 1] <- 1
wald_07 <- linda.wald.test(fit_07, L, model = "LM", alpha = 0.05)
rownames(wald_07) <- rownames(fit_07$output[[1]])

gt(data.frame(bins_tested = nrow(wald_07), bins_substrate_sig = sum(wald_07$reject),
              fraction_sig = round(mean(wald_07$reject), 3)))
bins_tested bins_substrate_sig fraction_sig
3239 987 0.305

30% of bins reject at padj <= 0.05.

substrate_vars_07 <- grep("^substrate", fit_07$variables, value = TRUE)
volc_07 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(substrate_vars_07, function(v) {
  o <- fit_07$output[[v]]
  data.frame(bin = rownames(o), substrate = sub("^substrate", "", v),
             log2FoldChange = o$log2FoldChange, pvalue = o$pvalue, reject = o$reject)
}))

ggplot(volc_07, aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(pvalue), color = reject)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ substrate, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey70", `TRUE` = "firebrick"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change vs Sediment", y = expression(-log[10](p))) + theme_bw()

top_07 <- volc_07[volc_07$reject, ]
top_07 <- top_07[which.max(abs(top_07$log2FoldChange)), ]

members_07 <- names(roll_07$bin)[roll_07$bin == top_07$bin]
tax_07 <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"))[members_07, ]
n_annotated_07    <- sum(is_annotated(tax_07))
n_multi_genome_07 <- sum(!is.na(tax_07$SharedGenomes))

The single largest shift, in either direction, is bin bin2 on PHBH Green vs. sediment: +10.4 log2 fold change at \(p =\) 4.0e-04. Its 43 members carry no shared lineage (this workbook has no GTDB call, data_curation_case_study2.Rmd), and 43 of 43 carries any curated call at all (MantisName, MicrobeName, a PlasticDB hit, or a depolymerase flag) – the table below has the specifics. 20 of the 43 members were independently assembled and binned in more than one sample’s GenomeID (the SharedGenomes column below).

info_07 <- data.frame(
  Protein = members_07,
  `Genome ID` = tax_07$GenomeID,
  `Shared genomes` = tax_07$SharedGenomes,
  `Mantis annotation` = tax_07$MantisName,
  `Microbe annotation` = tax_07$MicrobeName,
  PlasticDB = tax_07$PlasticDB,
  `Possible depolymerase` = tax_07$Depolymerase,
  `Length (aa)` = nchar(full_seq[members_07]),
  `Mean count, Sediment` = round(colMeans(cnt_da[md$substrate == "Sediment", members_07, drop = FALSE]), 2),
  check.names = FALSE
)
info_07[[paste0("Mean count, ", top_07$substrate)]] <-
  round(colMeans(cnt_da[md$substrate == top_07$substrate, members_07, drop = FALSE]), 2)
peak_07 <- pmax(info_07[["Mean count, Sediment"]], info_07[[paste0("Mean count, ", top_07$substrate)]])
info_07 <- info_07[order(-peak_07), ]
peak_07 <- sort(peak_07, decreasing = TRUE)
gt(info_07)

driver_07 <- info_07$Protein[1]
driver_annotated_07 <- is_annotated(tax_07[driver_07, ])
driver_desc_07 <- if (driver_annotated_07) {
  "does carry a curated call in this workbook -- see the table above for which one"
} else {
  "carries no `MantisName`, `MicrobeName`, `PlasticDB` or depolymerase call in this workbook"
}

top_share_07     <- peak_07[1] / sum(peak_07)
n_substantial_07 <- sum(peak_07 >= 0.1 * peak_07[1])
concentrated_07  <- top_share_07 >= 0.5

spread_desc_07 <- if (concentrated_07) {
  sprintf("It sits almost entirely in %s, detected in %d of 3 %s replicates and %d of 3 sediment replicates; the other %d members are near-zero traces in every sample, %s included, and contribute negligibly to the bin's summed abundance -- that protein %s%s.",
          driver_07,
          sum(cnt_da[md$substrate == top_07$substrate, driver_07] > 0), top_07$substrate,
          sum(cnt_da[md$substrate == "Sediment", driver_07] > 0),
          length(members_07) - 1, top_07$substrate, driver_desc_07,
          if (driver_annotated_07) "" else " -- the cleanest substrate-specific signal this differential-abundance pass found is also a member this workbook's own annotation pipeline said nothing about")
} else {
  sprintf("It is spread across the bin rather than concentrated in one protein: %s is the single largest contributor (%.0f%% of the bin's peak abundance) but %d of the %d members each reach at least a tenth of that -- a coherent multi-member signal, not a single-protein artifact. Its largest contributor %s%s.",
          driver_07, 100 * top_share_07, n_substantial_07, length(members_07), driver_desc_07,
          if (driver_annotated_07) "" else " -- unusual for a bin this well-supported; most of this workbook's dark proteins turn up alone, not as part of a mostly-annotated family")
}

Sorted by each member’s peak abundance, on whichever side of the contrast it is larger, the table shows the bin’s fold change: It is spread across the bin rather than concentrated in one protein: 15-2DG3_k141_360597_99 is the single largest contributor (14% of the bin’s peak abundance) but 19 of the 43 members each reach at least a tenth of that – a coherent multi-member signal, not a single-protein artifact. Its largest contributor does carry a curated call in this workbook – see the table above for which one.

Zb_07 <- Z[info_07$Protein, ]
S_07  <- 1 - as.matrix(proxy::dist(Zb_07, method = "cosine"))
dimnames(S_07) <- list(info_07$Protein, info_07$Protein)

df_07 <- as.data.frame(as.table(S_07))
names(df_07) <- c("i", "j", "TM_hat")
df_07$i <- factor(df_07$i, levels = info_07$Protein, labels = seq_along(info_07$Protein))
df_07$j <- factor(df_07$j, levels = info_07$Protein, labels = seq_along(info_07$Protein))

ggplot(df_07, aes(i, j, fill = TM_hat)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0.7, 1), name = "predicted\nTM-score") +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(x = "protein, table row above", y = "protein, table row above") +
  theme_minimal()

The floor is 0.813, comfortably above the 0.7 cutoff.

gt(data.frame(
  scope = c("whole protein universe", "substrate-significant bins only"),
  proteins = c(ncol(cnt_da), length(sig_members_07)),
  plasticdb_or_depolymerase_flag = c(sum(flagged[colnames(cnt_da)]), sum(flagged[sig_members_07])),

scope proteins plasticdb_or_depolymerase_flag pct
whole protein universe 30997 270 0.87

Conclusion

All three distances find substrate highly significant (\(p = 10^{-4}\), the ceiling of 9999 permutations), with diet – here, substrate – \(R^2\) of 0.437 for Bray-Curtis, 0.364 for Jaccard, and 0.541 for the representation. weightedRep leads both, by a larger margin than in the diet study (+0.104 over Bray-Curtis here against case_study.Rmd’s +0.072). All three pass the dispersion diagnostic (betadisper \(p > 0.6\) for every distance), so none of this is groups differing in spread rather than location.

The accession-sharing numbers (above) explain part of why protein identity does as well as it does here: this dataset sits between the diet study’s near-universal, single-database accession sharing and a fully private-accession regime – a real but partial minority of the catalog is shared across substrates, which is exactly the scenario where a protein-identity distance still has genuine signal to read, just less of it.

rollupStructural_thresholds() collapsed the 30997 proteins into 1887 bins at TM-score >= 0.5 and 7164 at >= 0.7; LinDA’s joint test rejected 32% and 30.5% of them respectively at padj <= 0.05 – substrate reorganizes abundance broadly across the structural repertoire under either clustering, the same qualitative picture the sample-level PERMANOVA gives, and neither threshold’s top hit is a low-power artifact of the other’s bin sizes: the largest shift at 0.5 is bin bin2 on PHBH Green (+9.5 log2FC), and at 0.7 it is bin bin2 on PHBH Green (+10.4 log2FC) – the same substrate at both thresholds. Curated PlasticDB/depolymerase flags are rare workbook-wide either way (270 of 30997 proteins, 0.87%); among substrate-significant bins they are carried by 0.82% at 0.5 and 0.92% at 0.7 – on the annotation this workbook happened to curate rather than a formal enrichment test either way.

This report does not repeat case_study.Rmd’s null-control battery (random-embedding, amino-acid-composition and length baselines) or its accession-masking shuffle test, so unlike that report it does not directly address whether the sample-level weightedRep signal, or the structural bins built on it, are separable from amino-acid composition or from how much samples happen to share literal protein calls. Both are a straightforward rerun of case_study.Rmd’s corresponding chunks against this dataset’s cnt/Z if that comparison is wanted.
